role.altitude: The administrative law judge keeps reading files, analysing law, weighing evidence, deliberating, deciding liability and explaining rights in person; repeating searches, checking whether rules changed, looking up rates and deadlines and retyping case details shrink.
skills_to_grow: Using saved searches and change alerts
Checking calculation modules against the statute
role.ambitious_version: A judge whose preparation time goes to the hard questions, with no software deciding anything.

tasks.short: Read the case file for legal questions, search legislation and precedent decisions, check that cited rules are current, research and analyze laws, regulations, policies and precedent decisions, discuss with the clerk, and write research notes.

steps.what: Judge reads the case file to identify the legal questions
Judge repeats searches in legislation and precedent databases for each case
Judge checks whether cited laws, regulations and precedent decisions are still current
Judge reads and analyzes the laws, policies and precedent decisions to determine conclusions
Judge discusses legal questions with the clerk or colleagues
Judge writes research notes for the hearing

tasks.design: Saved searches by legal issue and article number rerun on the licensed legislation and case-law base, instead of the judge building them again per case. An integration with the official legislation feed and the case-law database flags cited articles that were amended and decisions that were overturned or criticised, matched by article number and case identifier. No model reads, summarises or interprets; reading, analysing and discussing stay with the judge.
tasks.previous_blocker: Searches were rebuilt per case and currency was checked by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Saved searches and change feeds matched by article number.
tasks.still_hard: Policy rules that are published only as agency circulars.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing which precedent really fits the facts.
tasks.altitude: Less searching and checking; analysis stays.

reach.learn: Whether fewer outdated citations reach the draft.

evidence.claim: AI used by or for a judicial authority to research and interpret facts and law is high-risk under Annex III 8(a), so this design uses no model.
Legal research tools were wrong on over 17% and over 34% of 200+ queries.

assumptions: Boundary: legal research to prepare and conclude; preparing written decisions (task 7617) and reviewing claim documents (task 7618) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s3: about 70% of cited sources carry article numbers or case identifiers that the feed can match; s3 is priced at that share.
Reading, analysing, discussing and notes keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of policy rules outside the licensed base.
research_questions: Do outdated citations in decisions fall?

incremental.description: Judge maintains saved searches per legal issue.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: unusual legal questions; high: recurring issues with saved searches.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review the evidence, weigh it and apply the law, deliberate with the panel, look up rates and scales, calculate the amount, and record the determination of the existence and amount of liability.

steps.what: Judge reviews the available evidence in the case file
Judge weighs the evidence and determines the existence of liability under current laws and precedents
Judge deliberates with the panel members
Judge looks up statutory interest rates and penalty scales
Judge calculates the amount of liability, retyping amounts from the file
Judge records the determination in the case file

tasks.design: A calculation module in the case system holds the statutory interest rates and penalty scales and computes the amount from the amounts in the case record and the parameters the judge sets: period, rate and scale step. It replaces looking up tables and retyping amounts. The judge checks each result. Reviewing evidence, deciding liability and deliberating stay with the judge; the module only does arithmetic the judge orders.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rates were looked up in tables and amounts retyped into calculators.
tasks.enabler_now: Calculation modules with maintained rate tables.
tasks.still_hard: Amounts that depend on contested facts.

evidence.claim: Solely automated decisions with legal effect need a legal basis under GDPR article 22; here the judge decides and the module only calculates.

assumptions: Boundary: determining liability; recommending acceptance or rejection of claims (task 7621) and authorising payment (task 7624) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s5: amounts held as fields in the case record for about 70% of cases; s5 is priced at that share.
Reviewing, deciding and deliberating keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of cases with calculated amounts.
research_questions: Do corrections of calculated amounts on appeal fall?

incremental.description: Judge reports rate table errors to the module owner.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few calculated amounts; high: benefit and penalty cases with interest.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Decide whom to subpoena, prepare subpoenas, check and sign them, issue them, track responses, and administer oaths in preparation for formal hearings.

steps.what: Judge decides which witnesses or documents to subpoena
Judge prepares the subpoenas, retyping case details
Judge checks and signs the final subpoena
Judge issues the subpoena to the witness
Judge checks each subpoena for service and responses
Judge administers oaths at the formal hearings

approvals.approved_version: The subpoena for the named witness or documents, case number and hearing date, exactly as signed by the judge in s3, issued to the person named in it; any change needs a new signature.

tasks.design: A subpoena template in the case system fills parties, case number and hearing date from the case record and scheduling, instead of the judge retyping them. After the judge signs, the subpoena is issued as signed. A case view shows the service status and response of each subpoena, instead of the judge checking each one. Deciding whom to subpoena, signing and administering oaths stay with the judge.
tasks.previous_blocker: Case details were retyped into each subpoena and service was checked one by one.
tasks.enabler_now: Case systems with document templates and service tracking.
tasks.still_hard: Witnesses who must be served in person.
tasks.human_edge: Impressing on a witness what the oath means.

reach.learn: Whether subpoenas arrive with correct details.

evidence.claim: Case admin suits a records app with date rules and notifications, and drafting starts from templates.

assumptions: Boundary: subpoenas and oaths; scheduling hearings (task 21181) and conducting hearings (task 7625) are sibling tasks.
s2 saves retyping case details already in the record; s5 replaces checking each subpoena by hand.
Input contract for s5: service status recorded in the case system for about 70% of subpoenas; s5 is priced at that share.
Deciding, signing, issuing and oaths keep their full time.
research_questions: Do hearings postponed for missing witnesses fall?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few subpoenas; high: many witnesses per case.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Look up the appeal body and deadline, write and check the appeal-rights section, explain to claimants how they can appeal rulings that go against them, answer follow-up questions and refer claimants to legal aid.

steps.what: Judge looks up the appeal body, deadline and form for the decision type
Judge writes the appeal-rights section of the decision
Judge checks that the appeal section fits this claimant and ruling
Judge explains to claimants how they can appeal rulings that go against them
Judge answers claimants' follow-up questions about appeals in letters
Judge checks the claimant's details and decision date in the case system
Judge refers claimants to legal aid desks

tasks.design: The decision template inserts the fixed appeal-rights text for the decision type. Rules compute the appeal body, the deadline from the decision date and the form to use, instead of the judge looking them up and writing the section. Standard paragraphs from a plain-language appeal guide go into letters answering follow-up questions, and the judge writes the case-specific part. Checking the section, explaining in person and referring to legal aid stay with the judge. No model writes text for claimants.
tasks.previous_blocker: Appeal routes and deadlines were looked up and written per decision.
tasks.enabler_now: Decision templates with fixed appeal text and deadline rules.
tasks.still_hard: Decisions with several possible appeal routes.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining an appeal so a disappointed claimant actually hears it.
tasks.altitude: Less writing the same section; explaining stays.

evidence.claim: The appeal-rights text is fixed and belongs in a template, not a model draft.

assumptions: Boundary: explaining appeal rights; preparing the rest of the written decision (task 7617) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s1: deadline rules set for about 80% of decision types; s1 is priced at that share.
s2 saves writing the fixed text and computing the deadline per decision.
Checking, explaining and referring keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of decision types with several appeal routes.
research_questions: Do appeals filed late or at the wrong body fall?

incremental.description: Judge reports changes in appeal rules to the template owner.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: decision types with several routes; high: standard decision types.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
